rationale: Accept. All controls in the supplied records are accounted for and passed as designed: 23 total — 5 basic (reference, empty, recomputed, alternative, missing) plus 18 probes (13 wrong_solution, 5 valid_alternative); every wrong_solution failed exactly its targeted checks (with structure otherwise intact, no reliance on crashes or malformed files) and every valid_alternative passed all five. The public addendum matches the grader implementation: exact 9-column header and 9-field rows, blank-line/BOM/CRLF/quoting tolerance, all-or-none motif fields with chrom_2==chrom and strand in {+,-}, finite whole-base numerics, and two order-insensitive multisets over (chrom,start,end) and over all nine canonicalized row values, with full_row_multiset decisive — so no fragment-only, column-permutation, dropping or duplication shortcut passes. The numeric basis is demonstrated, not merely asserted: graded values are carried input annotations canonicalized to int when whole and compared as exact IEEE doubles otherwise, so 450/450.0/4.5e2 unify (executed: the independent stdlib 'alternative' run, executed without answer access, parses equal to the pandas-rendered reference, and valid-numeric-text) while 1-ULP, last-digit and rounding changes fail (executed: wrong-exact-values); there is no tolerance that could mask a wrong method. My previously listed points resolve to non-issues on closer reading: (a) placeholder text (0, -1, NA, nan) in place of empty always fails — 'NA'/'0' violate the chrom_2/strand validity rules in field_value_validity, 'nan'/'inf' violate finiteness (executed), and the only theoretical escape, a fabricated but internally valid motif record, necessarily fails full_row_multiset because the reference's motif fields are empty — so the public 'placeholders are not accepted' guarantee has no accepting path; (b) Python float() text leniency only canonicalizes value-equal spellings and cannot convert a wrong value into an acceptance; (c) the implicit stdlib csv field-size bound only affects files that must fail anyway (reported as a deterministic failure, never a crash) and cannot change acceptance of a reference-matching table; (d) the tie-rule and peak-population facts (earliest data line among tied maximal pvals; deduplicated peak records; annotation fragments) are not re-derivable from the output alone — the inherent, honestly-disclosed limit of an output comparator — and are corroborated here by the one executed independent implementation agreeing on the full 40,557-row parsed content via the passing 'alternative' control, plus the wrong-strongest-tie probe proving a wrong tie choice fails; the candidate records three further implementations as author-side validation claims, which I do not count as controller controls; (e) unexecuted hypotheticals (zero-byte file at the accepted location, gzipped/compressed file) fail deterministically via read_error rather than crashing, and I do not count them as controls because they were not executed. No answer leakage (the grader embeds only public contract facts — endpoint name, nine column names, strand domain; no row counts or measured values), no control-name/path/timestamp branching, always a valid JSON report with exit 0, and software choice remains open without a universal-portability claim (the two executed stacks — pinned bioframe/pandas reference/oracle and stdlib independent solution — are reported as instance evidence). The approved terminal artifact is the single graded endpoint and is fully covered by the decisive check; excluded notebook branches are plot-only diagnostics correctly left outside the contract. Suitable for subsequent packaging and its own isolation/oracle checks.
